mcqs.q: A salivary gland slide is identified mainly by its:
mcqs.explain: Microscopic identification relies on reading the acini (serous, mucous or mixed) and the duct system.

mcqs.q: Serous acini (e.g. parotid) are recognised by:
opts: Pyramidal cells with round basal nuclei, dark staining and a narrow lumen
Pale cells with a large lumen
Flat peripheral nuclei and pale cytoplasm
mcqs.explain: Serous acini are spherical, darkly stained, with pyramidal cells, round basal/central nuclei and a narrow lumen.

mcqs.q: Mucous acini (e.g. sublingual) show:
opts: Pale granular cytoplasm, flattened basal nuclei and a large lumen
Dark cytoplasm with central nuclei and a narrow lumen
mcqs.explain: Mucous cells have pale, granular cytoplasm with flattened, basally-located nuclei, forming large tubular acini around a large lumen.

mcqs.q: The PAROTID gland is histologically:
mcqs.explain: The parotid is a pure serous gland (with prominent ducts and fat infiltration).

mcqs.q: The SUBLINGUAL gland is histologically:
mcqs.explain: The sublingual gland is mainly mucous, with few striated ducts.

mcqs.q: The SUBMANDIBULAR gland is identified as a MIXED gland because it shows:
opts: Both serous and mucous acini, with serous demilunes
mcqs.explain: The submandibular gland contains both serous and mucous acini plus serous demilunes — the hallmark of a mixed gland.

mcqs.q: A serous demilune is best described as:
opts: A crescent of serous cells capping a mucous acinus
mcqs.explain: A serous demilune is a half-moon (crescent) cap of serous cells sitting on the periphery of a mucous acinus.

mcqs.q: The SMALLEST duct of the salivary duct system is the:
mcqs.explain: The intercalated duct is the smallest, lined by low cuboidal cells, with a diameter smaller than the acinar end piece.

mcqs.q: Striated ducts are lined by ___ epithelium and lie ___:
mcqs.explain: Striated ducts are simple columnar with basal striations (infolded membranes + mitochondria), located within the lobule (intralobular).

mcqs.q: Excretory ducts are located in the:
mcqs.explain: Excretory ducts run in the interlobular septa, are larger, and are lined by pseudostratified → stratified epithelium.

mcqs.q: The correct order of the salivary duct system (from acinus outward) is:
mcqs.explain: Saliva flows acinus → intercalated duct → striated duct (both intralobular) → excretory duct (interlobular).

mcqs.q: On H&E, which acini stain DARKLY?
mcqs.explain: Serous acini stain deeply/darkly (zymogen granules); mucous acini stain pale.

mcqs.q: The cells of a serous acinus are described as:
opts: Pyramidal, arranged around a narrow central lumen
mcqs.explain: Serous secretory cells are pyramidal, grouped around a narrow central lumen, with round basal nuclei.

mcqs.q: Intralobular ducts (intercalated + striated) are distinguished from excretory ducts because they:
opts: Lie within the lobule, not in the interlobular septa
mcqs.explain: Intercalated and striated ducts are intralobular (within the lobule); excretory ducts are interlobular (in the connective-tissue septa).

mcqs.q: Mucous acini tend to have a ___ lumen compared with serous acini:
mcqs.explain: Mucous acini have a larger lumen; serous acini have a narrow lumen.

mcqs.q: Which gland slide would show serous acini, many ducts AND fat (adipocytes)?
mcqs.explain: The parotid characteristically shows serous acini, many ducts and adipocyte (fat) infiltration.

mcqs.q: Adjacent to striated ducts, the histology often shows:
mcqs.explain: Striated ducts have numerous small blood vessels adjacent to them (supporting their ion-transport function).

mcqs.q: The cells lining the intercalated duct are:
mcqs.explain: Intercalated ducts are lined by low cuboidal to cuboidal cells and have a small diameter.

mcqs.q: A slide showing ONLY pale acini with large lumina and flat basal nuclei is most likely:
mcqs.explain: Pale acini with large lumina and flattened basal nuclei indicate a predominantly mucous gland — the sublingual.

mcqs.q: Larger excretory ducts may be lined by:
opts: Stratified cuboidal or stratified columnar epithelium
mcqs.explain: Smaller excretory ducts are pseudostratified; larger ones may be stratified cuboidal or stratified columnar.

saqs.q: How do you identify a serous gland (parotid) on a slide?
saqs.a: Pyramidal cells with round basal nuclei, spherical darkly-stained acini, and a narrow lumen; no mucous cells; prominent ducts and fat.

saqs.q: How do you identify a mucous gland (sublingual) on a slide?
saqs.a: Cells with pale granular cytoplasm and flattened basal nuclei, forming large tubular acini around a large lumen; pale staining.
Both serous (dark) and mucous (pale) acini, plus serous demilunes (crescents of serous cells on mucous acini).
A crescent-shaped cap of serous cells sitting on the periphery of a mucous acinus in a mixed gland.

saqs.q: List the salivary duct system from the acinus outward, with key features.
saqs.a: Intercalated (smallest, low cuboidal) → striated (columnar, basal striations, intralobular) → excretory (interlobular septa, pseudostratified/stratified, largest lumen).
Intralobular = intercalated + striated ducts (within the lobule). Interlobular = excretory ducts (in the connective-tissue septa between lobules).

saqs.q: Match each major gland to its acinar type.
saqs.a: Parotid = pure serous; sublingual = mainly mucous; submandibular = mixed (serous + mucous + demilunes).
